title: Pierce Brosnan reacts to Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond
text:

 Brendan Morrow USA TODAY Nov. 19, 2026 Updated Nov. 20, 2026, 9:10 a.m. ET Hear this story Pierce Brosnan is ready to pass the martini to a new 007.
 The former James Bond actor, 73, reacted on Nov. 18 to news that Robert Pattinson has been cast as the famed British secret agent. In an Instagram post, Brosnan shared a message of support to the "Twilight" actor alongside an edited photo of him as Bond.
 Brosnan and Pattinson have worked together before: They were costars in the 2010 romantic drama "Remember Me." Brosnan played the father of Pattinson's character in the movie.
 "Welcome to the world of Bond," Bronsan wrote. "You are going to be magnificent."
 Brosnan said he has "fond memories of our time together making 'Remember Me,'" and that "it has been a joy to watch you create a remarkable body of work and to go from strength to strength. Enjoy the ride."
 Love crosswords? Explore the Crossword page and play the new MidGrid Crossword. Brosnan starred as Bond in four movies, from 1995 to 2002: "GoldenEye," "Tomorrow Never Dies," "The World Is Not Enough" and "Die Another Day." He followed Timothy Dalton in the role and preceded Daniel Craig.
 Pattinson was officially unveiled as the next Bond on Nov. 16. He'll debut as the character in an upcoming movie by "Dune" director Denis Villeneuve. No release date or title has been announced. Alongside the casting news, a photo and video showing Pattinson as Bond, wearing a tuxedo and holding a gun, were revealed.
 "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson said in a statement. "To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement."
 Brosnan had previously weighed in on the next James Bond while the search was underway: He told Vanity Fair earlier in November that he is "just an audience member now" without any insider knowledge. "I'm just the man in the street who is eager to see who is going to play this epic role of cinematic history.
 Robert Pattinson named as James Bond actor in next 007 movie Robert Pattinson may actually be one of the older James Bonds James Bond needs Robert Pattinson more than he needs 007 Robert Pattinson's best James Bond-inspired suit looks over the years Robert Pattinson James Bond comments resurface after 007 casting All James Bond actors ranked from worst to first as new 007 is revealed "Whoever plays the role, I wish him the very best of life and strength and courage," Brosnan also told Vanity Fair. "You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond."
 While promoting "Remember Me" in 2010, Brosnan praised Pattinson, who then was in the middle of playing Edward Cullen in the "Twilight" film series, for the way he has handled fame.
 "With Robert Pattinson, I have watched this young lad really acquit himself very gracefully," Brosnan told IrishCentral in a 2010 interview. "He's doing allright with the pressure. He knows what to do and how to do it. It's a bit overwhelming for him at times. I mean he really did enter into the vortex of fame with the speed of a flame. So I think he's got it in control."
 Brosnan was the second former Bond to react to the casting. George Lazenby, the oldest living Bond actor, also sent a message of support on Instagram . The star, who played Bond in 1969's "On Her Majesty's Secret Service," said in a video addressed to Pattinson, "Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let's see if you have a 'this never happened to the other fella' moment. All the best, mate."
 Pattinson has also been receiving support from former costars and others throughout the industry.
 Rami Malek, a friend of Pattinson's who worked with him on "The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2" and played the Bond villain Lyutsifer Safin in "No Time to Die," told People magazine that he will be "quite extraordinary" in the role. "I've known Rob for quite some time and I could not be more proud," he said.
